title: Dizzy's 1948 European tour: the third-class cabins and the Shaw office
summary: Aboard the Swedish ship, Clarke discovered the Shaw office had put the band in third class despite a first-class contract, and the band forced them to pay the difference.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: MR. CLARKE: Diz, you know, he looked at me with that sly look, said, I got you, I knew I'd get you. So then we went to the Savoy Ballroom, with Chano Pozo and all that, and we formed -- I think it was the greatest band Diz ever had. And we made this famous trip to Europe with Chano Pozo and all. But what really happened on this trip, this trip, it made me realize that I didn't belong in the States. Well, what happened, this fellow, a Swedish fellow, who organized the tour, I had known him from 10 years before, in 1938. So we had travelled Third Class in 1938, which was my first trip. I was happy to be in steerage or anywhere, you know. But when we went to the pier and took the boat, and they assigned us to our cabins, then I saw a steward whom I had known 10 years before, Hans. We were riding on a Swedish ship, on the [Drottningholm.] So I -- and Lundquist had told me. He said, "This time, Kenny, it's in the contract. Everything first class from here out." He said, "It won't be like in '38. Everything first class." So I said, "Oh, Lundquist, that's beautiful." He said, "Dont't worry, this is

going to be really something," you know. So when we get on the ship, I see the Steward, and I said, "Hey, Hans, how are you?" He said, "Okay." And we hugged and everything. I said, "You're up in first class now." He said, "No, I'm still in third." I said, "You mean we're in third class." He said, "Yeah." So I asked Dizzy, I said, "Hey, Diz, man, you better look at your contract." So then all the other musicians began to follow me. They said, well, something's wrong because Kenny's up in the air and frothing at the mouth. Something's wrong, you know, so let's find out. They were following me around and peeping and listening. So Lorraine was in the cabin, so I said, "Listen, Diz, Lundquist told me that everything is first class." I said, "What are we doing here in third?" So Lorraine said, "Yeah, Diz, you'd better get that contract out and look at it." "Because," I said, "I know we're in third, because there's a Steward, Hans, I've known him for 10 years, and he can tell you we're in third." So he looked at the contract and it said first class. So what the Shaw office had done, they had raked off the top of the first class money and put us in third, because they figured, well, they don't know the difference.
Yes, sir. Then, after we straightened it out, and we made them pay us the difference of the third class -- now, I 'm the instigator of all this, because I couldn't stand it.
So we made them pay us the difference of first class. We said, 'Okay, we're assigned to our cabins, but we want that money, the difference.'
No, we got it on our way back.
Then, Lundquist had -- we had talked, because we were old friends from the trip with Edgar, you know?

And we had talked. He'd said, 'You won't have to work these days and you get paid extra for this.' So they had told us, 'Well, you get a flat salary, so much a week.' So I said, 'No, no, no, no.' I said, 'Look, Lorraine, let's go over it again, the contract.' So we read over the contract again and we found out we were supposed to get extra money for certain days, for so many days a week extra money, so it cost them something like a little over $20,000.00, that they had taken. Well, the son of Billy Shaw, Milt, was telling me, he says, 'Well --,' before all this happened, you know, before I saw -- had seen Hans, you know. He said, 'Well, I'm going to buy a nice new Oldsmobile when we get back, and you're going to be the first one I'm going to ride. You're going to be
the first one to ride in it." So I said, "Oh, yeah, nice, you know, nice." I hadn't dreamed that it was our money he was going to buy the Oldsmobile with.
